title: Seven Deadly Fitness Sins: Pride
summary: He argues pride is a virtue when it means self-belief that keeps you on the path and helps you lift others up. It becomes a sin when it turns into arrogance: deciding you have nothing left to learn, discouraging others, or using your talent to put people down, which he sees all over YouTube fitness.
claims: Confidence, self-assurance and even telling yourself you are the best are good when they keep you motivated; pride becomes a sin when used to attack others or make them feel worse
Telling yourself, as the Hagakure says, that you are the bravest warrior there is propels you and keeps your spirits high
If you keep telling yourself you are mediocre with no potential, that becomes your reality because you will never go after anything
Self-belief must coexist with objectively recognising when you are wrong, since there is always someone better
Deep confidence makes you immune to attacks and sets an example that people lacking confidence will copy
Much of the despair and toxicity among young men comes from lacking pride in their accomplishments, origins and country, which feeds the black pill
Like Netero says, a man who stops challenging himself is already dead; you are never done learning and there is no perfection
Pride turns into arrogance when people stop learning, encourage others to stop, or use their talent and status to crush others' dreams, which makes all their work worthless
YouTube fitness is full of people who think they are superior and should not be questioned
He tries to be open, believing he is not better than anyone and no one is better than him; both halves together are healthy pride
